Risk: Objective misalignment from unintended learning in physical human–robot interaction
Problem analysis: Human kinesthetic correction noise and bias in high-DoF robot arms
Theoretical insight: Restricting robot learning to a single feature per correction reduces misinterpretation
Design rationale: Sequential one-at-a-time learning strategy for online objective inference
Implementation mechanism: Heuristic selection of feature with largest induced change during correction
Implementation mechanism: Projected single-feature gradient update rule for weight update (Equation 10)
Validation evidence: Simulation with noisy human shows reduced unintended learning path length
Intervention: Deploy one-at-a-time objective learning algorithm during online physical corrections
